title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 55-56
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 55 to 56 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'जीवो विनयितासाक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 55 to 56 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 55 to 56.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 55 to 56** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **जीवो विनयितासाक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**जीवो विनयितासाक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः । अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः ॥** **अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः । आनन्दो नन्दनो नन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः ॥**

He is the living soul, the one who guides all and the witness. Mukunda, of boundless valour, is that God of gods. The treasure of the seas, the endless Self, the one who rests on the great ocean, and the one who ends all. Unborn, worthy of worship, great by his very nature is he. The conqueror of foes and the giver of joy is that God of gods. He is bliss itself, the one who delights us, true to dharma, and Trivikrama who measured the worlds.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 55 to 56 mean?
faq.a: He is the living soul, the one who guides all and the witness. Mukunda, of boundless valour, is that God of gods. The treasure of the seas, the endless Self, the one who rests on the great ocean, and the one who ends all. Unborn, worthy of worship, great by his very nature is he. The conqueror of foes and the giver of joy is that God of gods. He is bliss itself, the one who delights us, true to dharma, and Trivikrama who measured the worlds.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
